- Horizon prefers customer-managed keys if possible for at-rest encryption on production data.

Requested items / next steps:
1) Intro your security folks to ours (looped Rishi) so we can answer KMS/implementation specifics and fill out your vendor questionnaire.

Thanks Neha - appreciated the summary. A few quick notes from our security team: 

- SOC 2: We require a SOC 2 Type II report for platform vendors. If you can provide that under NDA that would be ideal.
- HIPAA: We will need a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) in place prior to any PHI processing.
- KMS/Encryption: Horizon prefers customer-managed keys when possible. Primary questions:
  * Can Redwood support customer-managed keys (BYOK) in a Dedicated or Private deployment?
  * What key management providers do you integrate with (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, on-prem HSMs)?
  * How is envelope encryption implemented and who holds the root key material?
  * Auditability: can you provide audit logs for KMS operations and key access?

We also have a vendor security questionnaire that we can share - I'll attach it and mark the sections on encryption. Tom (cc'd) is our security engineer and will jump on the call if we schedule.

Best,
Susan Lee
Head of Compliance Programs
Horizon Health
susan.lee@horizonhealth.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@horizonhealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-09-02T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security & KMS follow-up - post-call recap and next steps

Hi Susan - thanks for the clear list. A few direct answers and notes we can cover on the technical call: 

1) Customer-managed keys (BYOK):
- Hosted/Hosted-Dedicated: For our hosted offerings we can support CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) via cloud KMS integrations for Dedicated deployments where the customer owns the KMS key in their cloud account (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or GCP KMS).
- Private/on-prem: For Private deployments we support integration with customer HSMs (PKCS#11 or vendor-specific) and can operate in a BYOK mode where root keys never leave the customer environment.

2) Encryption at-rest and in-transit:
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 preferred) with mutual TLS available for Dedicated/Private peering.
- At-rest: AES-256-GCM for data at rest. We use envelope encryption where data keys are generated per-tenant/session and encrypted with a master key stored in the customer-managed KMS/HSM.

3) HSM support and key custody:
- We support AWS CloudHSM and commonly used HSM vendors for on-prem keys. For cloud-managed KMS (e.g., AWS KMS) customers retain administrative control of the CMK and can manage rotation/policies.
- For Private deployments, the HSM module stays under customer control; Redwood processes never have access to the raw root key material.

4) Auditability/logging:
- All key usage operations are logged and can be integrated with the customer's audit stream (CloudTrail/Stackdriver/Azure Monitor) for Dedicated/Hosted-in-customer-account setups.
- We can provide KMS operation summaries and attestations as part of the SOC 2 evidence package under NDA.

5) SOC 2 and evidence:
- We can provide a recent SOC 2 Type II report under NDA. For initial evaluation we can also provide our security overview and the KMS whitepaper (attaching). For full report access we typically use an NDA + secure link to the report.

Happy to walk through any of the above on the call. If Horizon has vendor questionnaire specifics, Neha - feel free to share and we'll start filling in answers (I can take the KMS/encryption sections).

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
